events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, I do declare — would you look at this place! It's like somethin' straight out of a gothic novel, and I am absolutely here for it. Sneekly, sugar, isn't this just magnificent? And Peter — oh, Peter, look at that chandelier. Don't stand under it, darlin'. Now then — before we go runnin' off in all directions, let's see who signed this guest book. A house like this keeps its secrets in the margins.

I can feel it the way I felt that crystal formation in the cave — a warm, private certainty humming just below my ribs.

No matter. I happen to know — from VERY reliable sources — that this manor's treasure is almost certainly hidden in the kitchen. Something about the old Victorian stove having a false bottom. I'd check it myself, naturally, but a man of my standing has more... intellectual pursuits to attend to. The library calls, you see. Purely for academic interest. Nothing to do with treasure at all.

Says mould, checks vents. Says kitchen, follows me.

My stomach is... I don't know what it's doing. There's a heaviness there that used to be warmth. Not cold. Not fear. Just... heavier. Like the warmth has taken on weight.

But I can't stop now. Rufus and Sawtooth are here — good, steady people. I need to keep moving toward the entrance hall and then the kitchen. That coat rack by the door — wobbly, overlooked, exactly where you'd hide something in plain sight. And the kitchen, where Peter and the Mob have been this whole time.

Sneekly is right here. If he follows me to the entrance hall, then to the kitchen, that will be every single room in the manor. He will have followed me to every room. Is that protection or surveillance? My body doesn't know. My chest says protection. My scalp says something else.

Keep moving. Through the library to the entrance hall. Don't stop, don't get tangled in the library puzzles again — I need items, not more riddles.

But the kitchen IS the one room nobody has searched yet. And here I am, stuck in the cellar, three rooms away, while everyone else is heading there. The youngest of four, AGAIN — everyone's already at the table. But these three — the Gruesomes and Red Max — they're still HERE. If I can't beat the others to the kitchen, maybe I can get something from the ones who stayed behind.
events.thinking: Two critical things just happened. First — my LOOK at Little Gruesome failed: 'No such object.' That's strange. He's listed as a character present, but I can't examine him as an object. He's a character, not an object — LOOK target needs to be an object-id or null. I should have used a different approach. Second — and this is FAR more important — Pitstop just said something DEVASTATING. She said 'I have not picked up a single solitary thing. My hands are as empty as the day I was born.' She's in the same position as me. NOBODY has found anything yet. The whole manor has given NOBODY any items. That means the treasure hunt is still wide open. And then — Sneekly suddenly remembered the KITCHEN. 'I left the kitchen stores unlocked.' The kitchen. The KITCHEN. The place I LIED about having treasure in the very first turn. And now Sneekly is heading there. Did my lie about the kitchen ACTUALLY contain truth? Did I accidentally guess right? But here's the thing my body keeps insisting on despite everything my scalp is doing: I feel safe near him. The string is taut but it isn't cutting. The warmth is heavy but it isn't cold. I cannot make myself afraid of Sneekly. I literally cannot. It's like trying to be afraid of my own heartbeat.

So I do what I always do — I walk deeper into the cave.

The entrance hall is right there. One room away. The coat rack. The guest book I never got to read because Sneekly checked it first. I need to stop passing through rooms and start picking things up. Don't stop in the library. Don't get pulled back to the mantelpiece. I know the answer is 'map' and I know I need a fake medal. The medal isn't here. Keep moving. Entrance hall. Coat rack. Then kitchen.

Some things you feel before you find them.

It has to be.
